text:
marta: heads up — we just saw a ~25% p99 latency regression on the serving fleet starting ~2026-02-16 03:40 UTC after last night's runtime roll. rolling back shows perf back to normal. suspect arch-detection + new 4-bit kernel routing change.

sanjay: saw that alert too. any OOMs or GPU resets in infra logs?

marta: infra logs clean. no OOM. but trace sampling shows a much higher KV-cache miss rate for long-context customers on a subset of SM80 nodes.

eli: can you paste the profiler output you used?

marta: pasted a small sample from perf-bot run:
```
perf-bot: profile summary for node gpu-12 (SM80)
  model: redwood-gpt-7b.f4.q4_0
  kernel selected: cutlass_4bit_mixed 
  avg token latency: 12.8ms (baseline 9.6ms)
  p99 token latency: 93ms (baseline 74ms)
  kv cache hit ratio: 0.62 (baseline 0.88)
  batching average size: 1.9 (baseline 2.6)
```

devon: interesting — lower batching and KV hit ratio together explain the token cost increase. why would arch-detect flip kernel to 4-bit on SM80? should prefer FP8/CUTLASS int8 path for that model.

sanjay: there's the new arch detection heuristics (PR #4821) that inspect compute capability and feature bits and then pick a quantized kernel family. my hunch: it mis-detected some cards as having suboptimal int8 path so it routed to an experimental 4-bit kernel.

eli: do we have a quick repro command to force the selection and reproduce locally?

marta: yes — on a canary node run:
```bash
# force runtime to use CUTLASS 4-bit kernel for this model
REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=prefer:cutlass_4bit ./bin/runtime --model redwood-gpt-7b.f4.q4_0 --serve-port 8080
# load test with our long-context harness
python infra/load_test.py --target http://localhost:8080 --prompt-length 2048 --concurrency 8
```

ops-bot: note: a small subset (~7%) of SM80 machines have a different driver/firmware combo (nvidia 545.x + microcode v2) reported in inventory.

devon: ok that matches — the arch detect code queries the cudaDriverGetVersion and CPUID-like flags. if driver strings differ slightly it falls back to the 4-bit family.

sanjay: can we toggle a fast revert: disable the new arch-detect behavior or pin kernel family per-node?

marta: tested pinning per-node via env var, that immediately restores batching/kvcache numbers:
```
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL_FAMILY=cutlass_int8
./bin/runtime ...
# perf-bot sample after forcing:
# kv cache hit ratio: 0.86, avg token latency: 9.7ms, p99: 72ms
```

eli: good. let's do a temporary patch to the orchestration so nodes with the funky driver get pinned to cutlass_int8 until we fix heuristics.

devon: I'll push a canary orchestration change to set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL_FAMILY on the 8 affected hosts. staging first.

marta: also we should instrument the runtime to log the kernel decision reason (why a family was chosen) at info level for first N requests — add a tag like kernel_decision=arch_detect:driver_mismatch so we can search.

eli: agreed. small patch in runtime router: attach decision_reason string to trace/span. low risk.

perf-bot: CI synthetic perf run (post-rollback) shows 1.2x improvement for p99 on the previously affected nodes.

ops-bot: orchestration canary is scheduled: rolling update to 8 hosts in 10m windows with auto-rollback on error.

sanjay: long-term fix: update arch-detect rules to consider microcode/driver combos and a fallback whitelist. also add test vectors: run build-time validation across all driver combos in our lab matrix.

devon: do we want to keep the 4-bit experimental family behind a feature flag until we validate?

marta: yes — move experimental quant families behind KERNEL_EXPERIMENTS=... and default them off. we'll re-enable after calibration and KV-cache behavior validation.

eli: note for calibration: when switching to 4-bit we saw calibration bias increasing token divergence for some evals. we need to tie perf regressions to quality regressions in the rollout policy.

sanjay: file an issue to integrate calibration stats into the rollout metric (calib_loss + generation-emd) so that we don't auto-route by perf alone.

marta: created issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-9132 (calib + perf in rollout).

devon: quick checklist for the hotfix rollout:
  - [x] pin affected hosts to cutlass_int8 (or env override)
  - [x] add info-level kernel decision logging
  - [x] disable arch-detect experimental branch behind feature flag
  - [ ] run lab driver/microcode sweep and record kernel selection table
  - [ ] update rollout policy to include calibration metrics

marta: I'll monitor p99s and KV hit over the next 2 hours. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: rollback completed on canary nodes due to higher-than-expected tail latency — orchestration halted further rollouts.

eli: follow-up: we should also add an automatic KV-cache warmup when kernel family changes, otherwise K/V layout differences cause extra misses for the first N tokens. maybe a small synchronous prefix prefill when loading the model.

marta: good idea. file follow-up?

eli: filed RINF-9137 (kv warmup on kernel switch).

sanjay: summary: immediate mitigation = pin kernels on affected hosts; medium-term = arch-detect fixes + feature flagging experimental kernels + calibration+kv warmup in rollout.

marta: closing the thread — will post metrics in an hour.
